decisions.reason: Its quantified government reference, close fit with the core aviation-security offer, and visible standalone commitment make a reversal very unlikely.

Even without published results, the firm has publicly backed it on a dedicated page and is likely to justify the investment by attributing slower uptake to temporary customer and regulatory conditions.
Because it leverages the firm's established training capabilities and can be bundled into existing contracts at low incremental risk, management is likely to retain it.
It supports the firm's push toward higher-value integrated security innovation, so an expanding firm in a growing market is likely to persist despite uncertain early traction.

It remains the most vulnerable because it is only lightly promoted and may be harder to commercialise, but management is still somewhat more likely to continue than to abandon an aviation-security initiative it has already backed.
